docs.doc_summary: This technical specification details the architecture and internal design of two core platform modules: the State Engine and the Agent Orchestrator. It defines the state management API, processing and storage layers, tenant configuration model, and full message processing flow, as well as the deterministic orchestration logic for agent triggering, prioritization, handoffs, and namespace-based write enforcement. The document provides concrete schemas, event models, and operational flows for building a reactive, state-driven multi-agent system.
key_topics: State Engine API and processing pipeline

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how session state is structured, validated, stored, and updated, or how agents are triggered, prioritized, and handed off within the orchestration layer. Especially useful for queries about trigger logic, discovery dimension handling, context assembly, state write boundaries, or end-to-end message processing flow.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not cover detailed LLM prompt design for individual agents, external integrations beyond storage and content safety, authentication/authorization mechanisms, frontend implementation details, or feedback model training logic.

top_sections.title: Module 1: State Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the State Engine as the coordination backbone of the platform, detailing its API surface, processing stages, tenant schema model, storage tiers, and complete state object structure.

top_sections.title: 1.5 Exact Message Processing Flow
top_sections.section_summary: Provides the full deterministic step-by-step pipeline for handling a user message, including NLU extraction, patch validation, merge logic, persistence, and event broadcasting.

top_sections.title: Module 2: Agent Orchestrator
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the deterministic orchestration layer responsible for agent activation, priority resolution, workflow transitions, and routing of outputs without using LLMs.

top_sections.title: 2.1 Agent Manifest System
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the manifest-based registration model that defines agent triggers, state needs, outputs, priorities, and discovery configuration consumed by the Orchestrator.

top_sections.title: 2.4 Handoff Manager
top_sections.section_summary: Details the transactional handoff process between core workflow agents, including confidence scoring, atomic operations, discovery dimension switching, and context preservation.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification details Module 3, the Knowledge Base (KB) Engine, which powers ingestion, intelligence extraction, structured storage, graph-based product reasoning, and multi-source retrieval for agents. It defines how unstructured content is processed via Foundry IQ, how structured intelligence is extracted and routed across custom stores, and how a proprietary Product Relationship Graph is built, maintained, and traversed. The document also covers caching, lifecycle management, confidence decay, and key architectural decisions for a scalable, tenant-isolated KB system.
key_topics: LLM-based content classification and intelligence extraction
Product Relationship Graph schema and confidence model
Knowledge base lifecycle management and document removal

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how documents are ingested, classified, indexed, and transformed into structured intelligence; how the Product Relationship Graph is built and scored; or how agents retrieve knowledge from multiple sources (Foundry IQ, graph, competitor store, patterns, playbooks). Especially useful for queries about retrieval reasoning levels, graph traversal logic, caching rules, and KB update or deletion flows.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define session state schemas, agent trigger logic, orchestration priorities, handoff mechanics, authentication, or frontend behavior. It also does not provide detailed prompt templates for individual agents.

top_sections.title: 3.1 Ingestion Layer
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the fan-out ingestion pipeline, including tenant-scoped storage, deduplication and versioning, Foundry IQ indexing, asynchronous classification, and metadata cataloging.

top_sections.title: 3.2 Processing Pipeline
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the LLM-powered content classifier, cross-KB intelligence extraction, routing to structured stores, and delegation of chunking to Foundry IQ.

top_sections.title: 3.4 Product Relationship Graph
top_sections.section_summary: Outlines the proprietary graph architecture, including schema, relationship types, four-layer automated graph building strategy, composite confidence model, and traversal logic.

top_sections.title: 3.5 Retrieval Layer — Multi-Source Query Orchestration
top_sections.section_summary: Explains how agents perform parallel fan-out retrieval across Foundry IQ, the product graph, competitor store, customer patterns, and playbooks, with agent-specific source mapping and query construction.

top_sections.title: 3.7 KB Lifecycle Management
top_sections.section_summary: Details how different KB components update, how document deletion cascades across derived intelligence, and how confidence decay is applied over time.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification defines Module 4: the Data Integration Layer, which ingests, maps, normalizes, deduplicates, enriches, and synchronizes external business data into the platform. It details the connector framework (CSV MVP and future CRM integrations), canonical schema and field mapping engine, transformation and deduplication logic, sync management (initial load, incremental sync, scheduler, DLQ), outbound write-back design, and the full end-to-end data pipeline with database schemas. The document establishes a connector-agnostic, tenant-isolated architecture that feeds clean data into the State Engine and KB Engine.
key_topics: Canonical schema and field mapping engine
Sync manager (initial load, incremental sync, scheduler, DLQ)

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how external CRM, ERP, or CSV data is ingested, mapped to a canonical schema, cleaned, deduplicated, enriched, stored, and synchronized within the platform. Especially useful for queries about CSV import behavior, sync scheduling, incremental updates, dead-letter queue handling, database schemas for accounts/transactions, or CRM write-back mechanics.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define session state processing, agent trigger logic, orchestration rules, or knowledge retrieval strategies. It also does not cover detailed LLM prompt design, frontend UX beyond CSV import screens, or authentication/authorization outside connector credential handling.

top_sections.title: 4.3 Field Mapping Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the canonical schema, mapping workflows, auto-suggestion model, and tenant-specific mapping persistence that translate external source fields into the platform’s standardized data model.

top_sections.title: 4.4 Transform & Normalize
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the normalization, deduplication, enrichment, and aggregation pipeline that converts raw mapped data into clean, analytics-ready records.

top_sections.title: 4.5 Sync Manager
top_sections.section_summary: Explains initial loads, incremental sync mechanisms (polling and webhooks), scheduling, reconciliation, and error handling via a Dead Letter Queue.

top_sections.title: 4.7 Outbound — Write-Back Service (Full Product)
top_sections.section_summary: Details CRM write-back capabilities, outbound field mapping, safety controls, idempotency rules, and audit logging for creating opportunities and logging AI activities.

top_sections.title: 4.8 Complete Data Pipeline Flow
top_sections.section_summary: Provides a step-by-step end-to-end walkthrough of the ingestion-to-enrichment pipeline, including mapping, validation, deduplication, commit, enrichment, aggregation, and downstream triggers.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification defines Module 5, the Multi-Tenancy & Tenant Configuration Framework that enables strict tenant isolation and deep per-tenant customization across the platform. It details row-level isolation with RLS enforcement, tenant-scoped configuration storage and versioning, business rules architecture, agent configuration controls, domain schema management, and a structured onboarding process with industry templates. The document establishes how a shared codebase supports multiple industries without code changes through JSONB-based configuration and controlled enforcement points.
key_topics: Row-level multi-tenancy with tenant_id and RLS
Business Rules Engine and rule schema
Domain state schema and discovery dimensions

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how tenant isolation is enforced, how per-tenant configuration (state schema, business rules, agent settings, UI branding) is structured and versioned, or how new tenants and industries are onboarded using templates and domain research. Especially useful for queries about rule enforcement timing, configuration rollback, and multi-tenant data separation.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define detailed session state processing logic, agent orchestration internals, knowledge ingestion pipelines, CRM connector mechanics, or LLM prompt engineering specifics beyond high-level configuration hooks.

top_sections.title: 5.1 Tenant Isolation Layer
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the row-level multi-tenant isolation strategy using tenant_id, compares alternative models, and details enforcement via middleware, PostgreSQL RLS, and query auditing.

top_sections.title: 5.3 Configuration Framework
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the tenant_config JSONB architecture, versioning model, caching strategy, and the evolution toward a self-serve Admin Portal configuration UI.

top_sections.title: 5.4 Business Rules Engine
top_sections.section_summary: Defines rule types, rule schema structure, enforcement timing in the execution pipeline, and onboarding sources for tenant-specific business logic.

top_sections.title: 5.6 State Schema Configuration
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the three-layer state architecture and how tenant-specific domain schemas and discovery dimensions are configured and managed.

top_sections.title: 5.7 Onboarding Flow — Complete Deep Dive
top_sections.section_summary: Outlines the 10-day onboarding timeline, required client inputs, degraded operational states, and industry template strategy for rapid time-to-value.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification defines Modules 6–11, the Core Agent Layer responsible for LLM-driven reasoning and conversation-facing outputs across six sales motions: Cross-Sell, Upsell, Full Solution, Renewal, Win-Back, and Net-New. It details agent-specific context assembly, trigger matrices, phase-aware output schemas (discovery → recommendation → action), prompt architecture, business rule enforcement, plugin activation, versioning, testing frameworks, and agent–orchestrator communication boundaries. The document establishes how agents operate as pure functions within a state-driven, multi-tenant architecture.

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how individual sales agents (M6–M11) generate discovery questions, recommendations, and action outputs; how phase transitions are handled; how prompts are structured and versioned; or how business rules are enforced within LLM-driven reasoning. Especially useful for queries about cross-sell/upsell logic, recommendation schemas, plugin activation, and agent–orchestrator boundaries.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define low-level state storage schemas, orchestration trigger priority algorithms, knowledge ingestion pipelines, CRM connector mechanics, or tenant isolation infrastructure beyond how agents consume configuration.

top_sections.title: 6.1 Context Assembly — How Each Agent Gets Different Context
top_sections.section_summary: Explains how the Orchestrator builds agent-specific context windows based on manifests, including state needs, graph traversal thresholds, enrichment data, KB retrieval, and token budgets for each sales motion.

top_sections.title: 6.3 Complete Trigger Matrix
top_sections.section_summary: Defines cold-start and mid-conversation triggers, re-trigger conditions, handoff mechanics, and activation rules for all six agents, formalizing deterministic workflow transitions.

top_sections.title: 6.5 Conversation Stages and Phase-Aware Output
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the three-phase model (discovery, recommendation, action) and how each phase produces a distinct structured JSON output schema consumed by the UI and orchestrator.

top_sections.title: 6.7 Prompt Architecture
top_sections.section_summary: Details the 9-section prompt template, business rule injection, tenant modifiers, structured output enforcement, and how prompts are assembled dynamically per agent and per turn.

top_sections.title: 6.10 Agent ↔ Orchestrator Communication Protocol
top_sections.section_summary: Defines execution flow, schema validation, rule post-processing, phase validation, and the strict separation of concerns where agents are pure functions and the orchestrator handles all I/O and state updates.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification defines Module 12, the Quick Action Agent SDK and plugin framework that enables built-in and custom plugins to run within the Orchestrator via a controlled Plugin Gateway. It details the SDK architecture, execution model, five-layer security isolation, manifest contract, scoped Platform Access APIs, structured UI rendering templates, inter-plugin communication, and full plugin lifecycle from development through monitoring. The document also specifies eight built-in quick action plugins, tenant customization controls, analytics integration with the Feedback Engine, and an evolution path from a controlled to an open plugin framework.
key_topics: Plugin Gateway and sandboxed execution model
Plugin manifest and Agent Interface Contract
Platform Access APIs (state, KB, LLM, history)
Structured UI rendering templates (Card, Table, Form, File)
Plugin Output Bus and inter-plugin communication
Plugin lifecycle, governance, and analytics integration

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how plugins are built, executed, secured, rendered, versioned, and monitored within the platform, including manifest design, SDK contracts, UI templates, inter-plugin communication, and custom plugin governance. Especially useful for queries about Quick Actions, Plugin Gateway behavior, sandboxing, and the built-in 8 plugin specifications.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define core session state schemas, deterministic agent trigger logic for core sales agents, knowledge ingestion pipelines, CRM connector mechanics, or low-level storage architecture beyond plugin-specific concerns.

top_sections.title: 12.1 SDK Architecture Overview
top_sections.section_summary: Introduces the Plugin Agent SDK as an interface contract executed inside the platform, describing the execution model, sandboxing, and how the Orchestrator invokes plugins through the Plugin Gateway.

top_sections.title: 12.2 Security Model — Five Layers of Isolation
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the defense-in-depth security architecture for plugins, including sandboxed execution, scoped APIs, namespace-restricted state writes, output sanitization, review gates, and resource limits.

top_sections.title: 12.3 Agent Interface Contract
top_sections.section_summary: Specifies the manifest structure, execute() and onFeedback() handlers, permissions model, resource limits, and output schema validation that govern all plugin behavior.

top_sections.title: 12.8 Built-In Quick Actions — All 8 Plugins
top_sections.section_summary: Details the eight built-in quick action plugins, including triggers, data requirements, LLM usage, output formats, and deployment strategy within the Orchestrator.

top_sections.title: 12.11 Plugin Lifecycle — Complete Deep Dive
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the end-to-end lifecycle for plugins—development, testing, registration, review, activation, rollback, and monitoring—with governance controls and analytics instrumentation.

docs.doc_summary: This technical specification defines the three interface-layer modules of the platform: Module 13 (Conversation UI), Module 14 (CRM Embedded Widget), and Module 15 (Admin Portal), along with their shared backend services. It details UI architecture, real-time WebSocket protocols, REST-based CRM embedding constraints, state-driven rendering, admin configuration surfaces, and cross-module access patterns. The document also formalizes transport decisions, authentication flows, and how frontend surfaces interact with backend modules M1–M20.
key_topics: Conversation UI architecture and state-driven rendering
WebSocket protocol and real-time message contracts
CRM embedded widget integration and write-back
Platform API and shared service layer

relevance_hints.best_for: Questions about how the frontend interfaces (Conversation UI, CRM Widget, Admin Portal) are structured, how they communicate with backend modules via WebSocket or REST, how CRM embedding and write-back work, or how admins configure business rules, agents, discovery dimensions, and integrations. Especially useful for routing UI-layer, transport protocol, session lifecycle, and admin configuration queries.
relevance_hints.not_useful_for: Does not define internal state schemas in depth (M1), detailed agent prompt logic (M6–M11), knowledge ingestion internals (M3), or low-level data normalization mechanics (M4). It focuses on interface behavior and integration patterns rather than core backend algorithms.

top_sections.title: Module 13: Conversation UI
top_sections.section_summary: Defines the real-time, state-driven Conversation UI including layout components, agent visibility, discovery tracking, recommendations, and its dependency on M1 and WebSocket updates.

top_sections.title: 13.2 Real-Time Communication — WebSocket Protocol
top_sections.section_summary: Specifies the WebSocket connection lifecycle, message types (server-to-client and client-to-server), and architectural rationale for real-time communication in the Conversation UI.

top_sections.title: Module 14: CRM Embedded Widget
top_sections.section_summary: Describes the CRM-embedded interface, including platform-specific context detection, REST polling constraints, compact UI components, and secure CRM write-back behavior.

top_sections.title: Module 15: Admin Portal
top_sections.section_summary: Outlines the administrative web application for configuring knowledge base content, integrations, business rules, agents, discovery frameworks, users, and analytics via REST APIs.

top_sections.title: Shared Backend Services
top_sections.section_summary: Explains the shared Platform API, WebSocket Service, and Auth Service that connect M13, M14, and M15 to backend modules with standardized routing, authentication, and scaling controls.
